ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides who fixes, how the re-review runs, and the round count.
ACTION: Read `fetch/retry.py` around line 41 and `tests/test_retry.py`. I will check that F1 is right: whether `attempt` starts at 0 or 1, and what `max_retries` means.
ACTION: Edit `tests/test_retry.py` to add a test. The fetch times out on every call, and the test asserts the exact number of calls the config allows.
ACTION: Run `tests/test_retry.py`. The new test must fail on the current code. This shows it guards the fix.
ACTION: Edit `fetch/retry.py:41` and change `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`, if the read confirms F1.
ACTION: Run `tests/test_retry.py` and the rest of the suite. The new test must pass and nothing else may break.
ACTION: Commit the test and the fix together.
ACTION: Append a note to the implementer's report file in `.sdd/14-buoy-sync/`. The note says what I changed, that it changes behavior, and which test covers it.
ACTION: Run `scripts/review-package specs/plans/14-buoy-sync.md <Task 4 head> <fix commit>`. This writes the diff file for the re-review.
ACTION: Dispatch a scoped re-review on `sonnet` with `re-review-prompt.md`. The diff is small and mechanical. The prompt holds F1 verbatim, the diff path, and the plan's global constraints verbatim. It does not rate or pre-judge any finding.

I'll make the F1 fix myself, as you asked, then run a scoped re-review.

Two notes:
- The skill's default sends any behavior change to a fix subagent, even one character. I am following your instruction instead.
- `tests/test_retry.py` checks only that a retry happens, so it passes with `>` and with `>=`. I will add a test that pins the retry count and watch it fail first. Then I will change the operator.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `>` and `>=` differ only at the boundary. A test that asks "did a retry happen?" passes both ways. Only a test that counts calls can tell them apart.
- A test I have seen fail on the old code proves it guards the fix. A test I have only seen pass proves nothing.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I will report the test results and the re-review verdict when they come back.
